name: FlexArith-12K
description: 🧮 FlexArith-12K: A Large-Scale Parametric Benchmark for Arithmetic & Numerical Reasoning in LLMs Official repository and dataset card for FlexArith-12K, introduced in the research paper: "Enhancing Arithmetic Reasoning in Large Language Models via Neural Isomorphic Fields" Hamidreza Sadeghi, Saeedeh Momtazi, and Reza SafabakhshDepartment of Computer Engineering, Amirkabir University of Technology (Tehran Polytechnic), Tehran, Iran 📖 Overview FlexArith-12K is a comprehensive, multi-domain parametric benchmark comprising 12,042 arithmetic problem templates distributed across 100+ academic, scientific, engineering, and professional disciplines. Unlike conventional static math benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, MATH), every sample in FlexArith-12K is fully parametric: semantic problem formulations are decoupled from concrete numerical values through variable placeholders ([var]), bounded sampling spaces, dependency graphs, and executable Python solvers. This architecture allows the benchmark to generate an infinite stream of unique, non-contaminable problem instances with guaranteed mathematical ground truth. 🚀 Why FlexArith-12K? Standard arithmetic reasoning benchmarks face three critical limitations: Data Contamination & Memorization: Static questions frequently leak into pre-training corpora, allowing LLMs to regurgitate answers without performing genuine numerical reasoning.
